annotation.method: Codex freshly reread the complete local paper for the missing-tier audit, surveyed every formal claim, excluded experiments and delegated textbook results, compared the candidates with the actual frozen NumStability source and Mathlib, and retained the earlier private neutral-proof finding that removed an overpackaged T3 candidate.

rejected_candidates.reason: It is a useful intermediate bound, but Theorem 3.2 strictly extends it by treating inputs not already in the low precision.
It is explicitly a direct application of Theorem 3.1 and is less central than the selected input-conversion and LU-solve assemblies.
Its two conclusions are delegated to Higham's textbook Theorems 9.3 and 8.5 rather than proved in this paper.
An end-to-end formalization overlaps the frozen NumStability block-LU factorization infrastructure and would give L a material shortcut, so it cannot serve as T3.

When Theorem 4.3's factorization bound and the two triangular-solve bounds are supplied as assumptions, the remaining nearby-system proof is only routine perturbation assembly. Deriving those bounds instead would overlap frozen NumStability block-LU and triangular-solve results, so the paper does not support a qualifying T3 replacement.
The probabilistic statement is imported from another paper and the remaining comparisons use first-order or approximate language rather than exact finite claims.
They are empirical measurements rather than proof targets.

T1.decision: Derive Algorithm 3.1's full indexed factorization and equation (3.4) from recurrence (3.1), local model (3.2), and effective roundoff (3.3), retaining the distinct effective/internal gamma factors, q+b-1 right-to-left refinement, and zero-alpha same-precision specialization.

T2.decision: Skipped after a fresh complete-paper reread and frozen-source comparison. Theorem 3.2 reuses the same one substantial product-accumulation theorem as T1; its input-conversion perturbation assembly is short and supplies no second substantial NumStability result. Theorems 4.3 and 4.4 can use several library results only by moving into the block-LU and triangular-solve arguments, but the latter solve results are delegated to textbook theorems rather than proved in this paper, so they do not give a source-faithful T2.

T3.decision: Skipped after private re-audit: Theorem 4.4 is easy if its factorization and solve bounds are assumptions, while deriving those bounds end to end overlaps substantial frozen NumStability block-LU and triangular-solve results and would make L faster than N. No other proved result in the paper is both T2-level difficult and free of a useful NumStability counterpart.

selection_policy: Use a finite claim made and proved in this paper.
Reject experiments, speed estimates, vague asymptotics, and claims whose proof is mainly delegated elsewhere.
Prefer exact displayed bounds and identities.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after verified frozen-library searches.
